action: Called Stephanie Morris for 60-day gate verdict; formally closed sale-inquiry path; called Kevin O'Brien to reactivate EV charger loan; got business insurance quote from Priya; checked with Betty Kowalski on logistics scouting activity
narrative: Stephanie Morris gave Amir the honest answer: she found one party genuinely interested in the property — a regional last-mile delivery operator — but their ceiling was $255,000, well below the $300,000 floor Amir had set. No buyer materialized at the threshold he required. Amir honored his own framework: he closed the sale-inquiry path formally, thanked Stephanie, and confirmed the $350 valuation fee for payment. He called Kevin O'Brien at the bank and reactivated the $12,000 capital improvement loan; Kevin confirmed the rate and terms are still valid and scheduled a document-signing appointment for next week. Priya Sharma provided a business interruption and general liability quote — around $280 per month for combined coverage — and Amir committed to starting the policy, finally closing an insurance gap that has been open for the entire simulation. Betty Kowalski confirmed she had heard nothing from logistics or delivery operators scouting Auto Row properties, which was consistent with Stephanie's finding that the buyer demand is thinner than the thesis required.
